fact: The government portal reports that under the Stratégie nationale Togo Digital 2025 181 classrooms were connected through the ENT, reaching 8,500 pupils, and over 1,000 computers, printers and projectors were installed in scientific secondary schools, run jointly by the education and digital transformation ministries; counts of activity, measured against no target of the strategy, and dated by the article's publication date, 2026-05-04, as the document gives no event date.

The Global Fund's Office of the Inspector General, auditing Togo's health supply-chain digitalisation, states there is an 'absence of coordinated national digitalization strategy' amid multiple digitalisation initiatives; the document gives no audit date other than its publication date, 2025-06-04, which is used here.

WeAreTech.Africa reports that the government, through the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation, 'recently launched' a recruitment to select a consultant to draft the next national digital strategy, called Togo Digital 2025-2030, which updates the strategic framework set up in 2020; no adopting act is given; dated by the article's publication date, 2025-05-28.

The article says the previous strategic framework of 2020 had enabled notable advances, naming the e-Gouv government platform, digital service centres and cybersecurity and data protection laws, with no target or report cited; dated by the article's publication date, 2025-05-28.

At the opening of the Lomé data centre on 2021-06-08 the Minister of the Digital Economy and Digital Transformation referred to 'the 2020-2025 roadmap', a stated period that covers that date; the article describes no scope for the roadmap and does not say whether its text is published. Text public: not stated.

The World Bank project paper says that in December 2020 a consulting firm was recruited to help the Government of Togo elaborate its Togo Digital Strategy 2025, a strategic study to inform accelerated digital transformation in the country, expected to be completed by summer 2021; no adopting act is mentioned.

The paper says the technical assistance to deliver the Togo Digital Strategy 2025 is financed under the World Bank's WARCIP project: the winning bid was US$1.36 million against a US$0.6 million budget, and the additional financing covers a US$1.0 million overrun; this is the cost of preparing the strategy, dated by the paper's publication date, 2021-04-29.

The paper says the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation (MDEDT) is the body that identified added needs and wants to amend the contract to widen the scope of the Togo Digital Strategy 2025 study (about US$200,000 more); no act or the strategy mandates it, dated by the paper's publication date, 2021-04-29.

The April 2021 presentation by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation (MENTD) says it forms part of the elaboration of the Togo Digital 2025 strategy, whose definition of a strategic roadmap 'a été lancé', with three parts (foundations of digital transformation, digitalisation of public and social services, creation of a digital economy) and nine programmes; no adopting act is given.

The presentation says that in the portfolio identified for the Togo 2025 strategic plan the MENTD leads 6 projects and 1 reform and supports 21 projects and 3 reforms, and that the plan sets it three priority objectives (digitalise state services, make Togo a digital hub, give all citizens internet access); no act is cited.

Togo Officiel reports that the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation launched on 22 May 2025 the recruitment of a consultant to update the national digital transformation strategy as a new 'Togo Digital' strategy; it is being prepared, not yet issued.
The new 'Togo Digital' strategy is to cover 2025-2030, per Togo Officiel.
The ministry started recruiting a consultant on 22 May 2025 to write the successor strategy Togo Digital 2025-2030.

Togo Officiel says the current strategy, the country's first digital transformation strategy of about five years ago, ends at the end of 2025; the date used is the article's publication date, 2025-05-27.

In his independence address the President says Togo 'a adopté' a strategy called Stratégie Togo Digital 2025, resting on three axes and aiming at lasting digital transformation, including progressive digitisation of administrative procedures; no act or adoption date is given, so the address date is used.
